The Transformer architecture was initially shown to be effective for machine translation (Vaswani et al., 2017). It has since been used in a wide variety of NLP settings, including but not limited to language modeling (Radford et al., 2018; Al-Rfou et al., 2019) and classification tasks (Devlin et al., 2018; Yang et al., 2019).

The primary building block of the Transformer is self-attention (Cheng et al., 2016). Self-attention processes a sequence by replacing each element with a weighted average of the rest of the sequence.

Overall, our implementation closely follows its originally proposed architecture and refers readers to the original paper (Vaswani et al., 2017) for a more detailed introduction.
reference: The Transformer is a neural network architecture based entirely on attention mechanisms. It uses an encoder-decoder structure and avoids recurrence and convolution, allowing greater parallelization during training.

response:
Self-attention is an attention mechanism that relates different positions of a single sequence to compute a representation of the sequence. It has been used successfully in various tasks, including reading comprehension, abstractive summarization, textual entailment, and learning task-independent sentence representations.

In the Transformer model, self-attention is used as a way for each position in the encoder (or decoder) to attend over all positions in the previous layer (in the case of the encoder), or up to and including that position itself. This allows every position in the sequence to be considered when computing the representation.

The output of the final decoder block is fed into a dense layer with a softmax output, whose weights are shared with the input embedding matrix. All attention mechanisms in the Transformer are split up into independent "heads" whose outputs are concatenated before being further processed.

Self-attention can attend over long distances due to its linear or logarithmic scaling mechanism, but this makes it more difficult to learn dependencies between distant positions. To counteract this effect, Multi-Head Attention is used as described in section 3.2, which reduces the effective resolution while allowing for more dependencies to be learned.

In addition, relative position embeddings (Shaw et al., 2018; Huang et al., 2018a) have become more common, providing an explicit position signal to the Transformer.
reference: Self-attention allows each position in a sequence to attend to other positions in the same sequence. It calculates attention weights based on queries, keys, and values, allowing the model to focus on relevant tokens.
